declarations.name: bornagain
declarations.description: Restores a deleted character to an account.
declarations.usage:
deletedCharID(, newCharName)(, accountName)
Given the ID of a deleted character, this command restores that character to its owner.  (You can find the ID of a deleted character using the @finger command.)
If the deleted character's name has since been taken by a new character, you can specify a new name for the restored character as the second parameter.  (You can find if the name has been taken by also using the @finger command.)  Use a comma to separate the arguments.
If needed, you can specify an account name as a third parameter if the character should be restored to an account other than its original owner.  Again, use a comma between the arguments.

declarations.name: create
declarations.description: Creates an object or objects in the world.
declarations.usage:
<wcid or classname> (amount) (palette) (shade)
This will attempt to spawn the weenie you specify. If you include an amount to spawn, it will attempt to create that many of the object.
Stackable items will spawn in stacks of their max stack size. All spawns will be limited by the physics engine placement, which may prevent the number you specify from actually spawning.Be careful with large numbers, especially with ethereal weenies.

declarations.name: createliveops
declarations.description: Creates an object or objects with lifespans in the world for live events.
declarations.usage:
<wcid or classname> (amount) (lifespan) (palette) (shade)
This will attempt to spawn the weenie you specify. If you include an amount to spawn, it will attempt to spawn that many of the object.
Stackable items will spawn in stacks of their max stack size. All spawns will be limited by the physics engine placement, which may prevent the number you specify from actually spawning.
Be careful with large numbers, especially with ethereal weenies.
If you include a lifespan, this value is in seconds, and defaults to 3600 (1 hour) if not specified.

declarations.name: qst
declarations.description: Query, stamp, and erase quests on the targeted player
declarations.usage:
(fellow) [list | bestow | erase]
qst list - List the quest flags for the targeted player
qst bestow - Stamps the specific quest flag on the targeted player. If this fails, it's probably because you spelled the quest flag wrong.
qst stamp - Stamps the specific quest flag on the targeted player the specified number of times. If this fails, it's probably because you spelled the quest flag wrong.
qst erase - Erase the specific quest flag from the targeted player. If no quest flag is given, it erases the entire quest table for the targeted player.

declarations.name: reportbug
declarations.description: Generate a Bug Report
declarations.usage:
<category> <description>
This command generates a URL for you to copy and paste into your web browser to submit for review by server operators and developers.
Category can be the following:
Creature
NPC
Item
Quest
Recipe
Landblock
Mechanic
Code
Other
For the first three options, the bug report will include identifiers for what you currently have selected/targeted.
After category, please include a brief description of the issue, which you can further detail in the report on the website.
Examples:
/reportbug creature Drudge Prowler is over powered
/reportbug npc Ulgrim doesn't know what to do with Sake
/reportbug quest I can't enter the portal to the Lost City of Frore
/reportbug recipe I cannot combine Bundle of Arrowheads with Bundle of Arrowshafts
/reportbug code I was killed by a Non-Player Killer
